entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Şehzade Korkut was an Ottoman prince who served as regent for the Ottoman throne from 1502 to 1503, briefly holding power after the death of his father Sultan Bayezid II. This event had significant regional consequences, as it led to the ascension of his cousin, Selim I, who would go on to expand the Ottoman Empire into the Middle East and North Africa. The regency of Şehzade Korkut marked the beginning of a period of Ottoman consolidation and modernization under the Yavuz Sultan Selim, who would implement significant reforms and strengthen the empire's military and administrative structures. This legacy can be seen in the subsequent development of the Ottoman Empire into a major world power, with far-reaching impacts on global politics, culture, and society. Şehzade Korkut's reign also highlights the complex web of alliances and rivalries within the Ottoman court, as he navigated the treacherous landscape of Ottoman politics to secure his position and protect his family's interests. Ultimately, Şehzade Korkut's time in power was cut short, and he died in 1513, but his legacy as a key figure in Ottoman history has endured for centuries.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Şehzade Korkut's regency marked the beginning of a period of Ottoman consolidation and modernization under the Yavuz Sultan Selim, who would go on to expand the empire into the Middle East and North Africa, leaving a lasting legacy in Ottoman history.
